headline: This law requires anglers fishing for reef fish in the Gulf of Mexico to carry tools that help release fish at depth, and orders studies on fish discard deaths.
what_it_does: Fish caught from deep water can suffer barotrauma, a pressure injury that often kills them after release. The law requires commercial and recreational fishermen fishing for reef fish in the Gulf of Mexico Exclusive Economic Zone to have a venting tool or descending device rigged and ready to use. It also directs the Department of Commerce to contract with the National Academy of Sciences for a study and report on discard mortality, and directs Commerce and the Gulf of Mexico Fishery Management Council to create reporting guidance and a plan to assess how well these devices work and how often they are used.

who_it_affects.group: Commercial fishermen targeting reef fish in the Gulf of Mexico
who_it_affects.how: They must have a venting tool or descending device rigged and ready for use when fishing for reef fish in the federal Gulf waters.

who_it_affects.group: Recreational anglers fishing for reef fish in the Gulf of Mexico
who_it_affects.how: They must have a venting tool or descending device rigged and ready for use when fishing for reef fish in the federal Gulf waters.

who_it_affects.group: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Department of Commerce
who_it_affects.how: They must arrange a National Academy of Sciences study on reef fish discard mortality and help develop reporting guidance and an effectiveness plan for barotrauma-reducing devices.

who_it_affects.group: Gulf of Mexico Fishery Management Council
who_it_affects.how: It must help develop guidance for reporting discards and a plan to assess the effectiveness and use of barotrauma-reducing devices.
